chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala ibn Ayyub from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in killing ants and lice in the Haram (sanctuary)."

key_terms.بَأْسَ: Harm or penalty (usually referring to expiation/kaffarah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing ants and lice while in the state of Ihram in the Haram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the chapter on expiation for unintentional violations, clarifying that the sanctity of the Haram does not extend to small, non-annoying insects like ants and lice. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle that the prohibition of killing game or specific creatures in the sanctuary is limited to those of significance, thereby allowing pilgrims to maintain hygiene without incurring the financial penalty (kaffarah) associated with major transgressions.
